title: Master of Computer Applications | AITM Bhatkal
text:
The Department of Master of Computer Applications (MCA) is committed to nurturing skilled IT professionals equipped with strong technical expertise and industry-oriented knowledge.
The department offers a comprehensive curriculum covering advanced computing, software development, data analytics, networking, and emerging technologies.
With a focus on practical learning, innovation, and research, the MCA program prepares students to meet the evolving demands of the global IT industry.
To become a center of excellence in computer education and research, producing competent professionals who contribute to technological advancement and societal development.
Mission
1. To provide high-quality education in computer applications through innovative teaching and learning practices.
2. To foster a culture of research, creativity, and critical thinking among students.
3. To build industry-ready graduates equipped with modern technical skills and professional ethics.
4. To encourage continuous learning and adaptability to emerging technologies.
Program Educational Objectives (PEOs)
PEO 1 Professional Competence: Graduates will develop strong technical knowledge and problem-solving skills to design, develop, and implement efficient computer-based solutions in diverse IT domains. PEO 2 Employability and Innovation: Graduates will be employable in the software industry, capable of adapting to emerging technologies, and motivated to innovate through continuous learning. PEO 3 Leadership and Teamwork: Graduates will demonstrate effective communication, teamwork, leadership qualities, and project management skills. PEO 4 Ethics and Social Responsibility: Graduates will practice ethical principles, professionalism, and social responsibility while addressing real-world challenges. PEO 5 Research and Lifelong Learning: Graduates will engage in research, higher studies, or entrepreneurial pursuits by applying analytical thinking and creativity.
Program Outcomes (POs)
PO1 Foundation Knowledge: Apply knowledge of mathematics, programming logic and coding fundamentals for solution architecture and problem solving. PO2 Problem Analysis: Identify, review, formulate and analyze problems primarily focusing on customer requirements using critical thinking frameworks. PO3 Development of Solutions: Design, develop and investigate problems with an innovative approach incorporating ESG/SDG goals. PO4 Modern Tool Usage: Select, adapt and apply modern computational tools with an understanding of limitations including human biases. PO5 Individual and Teamwork: Function and communicate effectively as an individual or a team leader in diverse and multidisciplinary groups using agile methodologies. PO6 Project Management and Finance: Use the principles of project management such as scheduling and work breakdown structure, and principles of Finance for profitable project management. PO7 Ethics: Commit to professional ethics in managing software projects. Use new technologies for cyber security and insulate customers from malware. PO8 Life-long Learning: Change management skills and the ability to learn, keep up with contemporary technologies and ways of working.
Program Specific Outcomes (PSOs)
PSO 1: Enable students to apply the computing and soft skills acquired in the MCA program to develop innovative applications for the betterment of society. PSO 2: Provide exposure to techniques that would enable students to design, implement, and evaluate IT solutions. PSO 3: Enable students to meet the challenges of research and development in computer science and applications.

About This Department
About Us
The Department of Computer Science and Engineering (CSE) at Anjuman Institute of Technology and Management is committed to providing high-quality education that blends strong theoretical foundations with modern technological skills.
The department focuses on nurturing innovative thinkers, problem solvers, and future-ready professionals capable of meeting global industry demands.
With a curriculum aligned to emerging trends, the department offers two specialized undergraduate programs in addition to the core CSE stream: CSE in Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning (AIML) and CSE in Data Science.
These programs provide students with advanced knowledge in AI technologies, machine learning algorithms, big data analytics, data visualization, cloud computing, and intelligent systems.
A notable strength of the department is its VTU-affiliated Research Centre, which serves as a platform for scholars to pursue research leading to Ph.
D. degrees. The centre actively promotes high-quality research, publications, and innovative projects across various domains of computer science.
Department Information
Vision
The Department of Computer Science and Engineering at AITM envisions emerging as a centre of excellence in technical education, research, and innovation. We aim to nurture highly skilled, industry-ready, and socially responsible computer engineers equipped with strong theoretical foundations, practical competence, and ethical values. Our vision is to create a vibrant learning ecosystem that embraces emerging technologies such as Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Cybersecurity, Data Science, Cloud Computing, and the Internet of Things. The department aspires to develop globally competent graduates who demonstrate leadership, professionalism, and a commitment to societal development.
Mission
The mission of the Department of Computer Science and Engineering at AITM is to impart high-quality technical education that equips students with strong analytical abilities, sound engineering principles, and practical skills. We strive to develop competent professionals through a curriculum that emphasizes outcome-based learning, hands-on experience, and continuous improvement. We are committed to fostering a culture of research, innovation, and entrepreneurship by encouraging engagement in creative problem-solving, interdisciplinary projects, and emerging technologies such as AI, ML, Cybersecurity, and Data Science. The department aims to build responsible engineers who uphold ethical values, demonstrate leadership qualities, and contribute meaningfully to society.

title: Electronics & Communication Engineering | AITM Bhatkal
text:
Established in 1985, the Department of Electronics and Communication Engineering at AITM has been committed to academic excellence and innovation.
With a vision to achieve national recognition, the department offers a strong learning environment supported by modern infrastructure and advanced laboratories in IoT, Embedded Systems, DSP, VLSI, Communication, and Antenna Systems.
Our department embraces modern teaching-learning practices and has developed a dynamic curriculum designed to meet the evolving needs of students and industry.
Our faculty actively engage in research, offering vibrant opportunities with PhD programs.
We are committed to empowering future leaders through technology, promoting creativity and innovation via student projects, ideation workshops, hands-on sessions on latest technologies, industry internships and interdisciplinary projects.
To be a leading Electronics and Communication department that provides excellent technical education, conducts impactful research, and produces globally competent engineers who contribute to society and technological advancement.
Mission
1. Offering comprehensive education that blends theoretical understanding with practical skills.
2. Fostering innovation, research, and entrepreneurship.
3. Upholding ethical standards and encouraging sustainable societal development through engineering solutions.
Program Educational Objectives (PEOs)
PEO 1: Graduates will demonstrate technical competence in Electronics & Communication and apply engineering principles to real-world problems. PEO 2: Graduates will develop professional skills such as effective communication, teamwork, leadership, and ethical responsibility. PEO 3: Graduates will engage in lifelong learning, adapting to evolving technologies and contributing to innovation and research. PEO 4: Graduates will act with social responsibility and contribute positively to societal development through their professional practice.
Program Outcomes (POs)
PO1 Engineering Knowledge: Apply the knowledge of mathematics, science, engineering fundamentals, and computer science to the solution of complex engineering problems. PO2 Problem Analysis: Identify, formulate, review research literature, and analyze complex engineering problems using first principles. PO3 Design/Development of Solutions: Design solutions for complex engineering problems with appropriate consideration for public health, safety, and environmental factors. PO4 Conduct Investigations of Complex Problems: Use research-based knowledge including design of experiments, analysis and interpretation of data. PO5 Modern Tool Usage: Create, select, and apply appropriate techniques and modern engineering tools to complex engineering activities. PO6 The Engineer and Society: Apply reasoning to assess societal, health, safety, legal and cultural issues relevant to professional engineering practice. PO7 Environment and Sustainability: Understand the impact of engineering solutions and demonstrate knowledge of sustainable development. PO8 Ethics: Apply ethical principles and commit to professional ethics and responsibilities. PO9 Individual and Team Work: Function effectively as an individual and as a member or leader in diverse teams and multidisciplinary settings. PO10 Communication: Communicate effectively on complex engineering activities with the engineering community and society at large. PO11 Project Management and Finance: Demonstrate knowledge of engineering and management principles and apply these to manage projects. PO12 Life-long Learning: Recognize the need for independent and life-long learning in the broadest context of technological change.
Program Specific Outcomes (PSOs)
PSO 1: Designing, analyzing and implementing engineering solutions using specialized knowledge in Electronics & Communication. PSO 2: Proficient use of modern tools, software, and equipment relevant to ECE practice. PSO 3: Working in multidisciplinary environments integrating ECE with other engineering domains.

title: Basic Science & Humanities | AITM Bhatkal
text:
The Department of Basic Science and Humanities (BSH) at AITM, Bhatkal, serves as the academic foundation for all engineering programs and plays a crucial role in shaping the intellectual and professional growth of first-year students.
The department integrates the core disciplines of Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry, English, and Humanities to build strong conceptual foundations that support advanced engineering studies across all branches.
The BSH Department is committed to instilling scientific temperament, analytical thinking, problem-solving skills, effective communication, and ethical values — all essential qualities for modern engineers.
To promote innovation and hands-on learning, the department offers modern technical workshops introducing students to emerging technologies early in their academic journey: Arduino programming, Python bootcamps, Laser Cutting, and 3D Printing through the Innovation Lab.
To create a strong academic foundation that develops globally competent engineering graduates with scientific knowledge, mathematical insight, communication excellence, ethical values, and a passion for innovation.
Mission
1. To impart high-quality foundational education in Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry, English, and Humanities.
2. To cultivate scientific thinking, logical reasoning, creativity, and problem-solving skills among engineering students.
3. To promote hands-on learning, research aptitude, and innovation through technical workshops and modern laboratory facilities.
4. To enhance communication skills, ethical values, and professional behavior necessary for engineering practice.
5. To create an inclusive, encouraging environment that supports student success and holistic development.
Program Educational Objectives (PEOs)
PEO 1 Strong Fundamental Knowledge: Develop a solid understanding of core concepts in Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry, and Humanities that forms the analytical and scientific base for advanced engineering studies. PEO 2 Problem-Solving and Analytical Ability: Apply mathematical techniques, scientific reasoning, experimental skills, and logical thinking to identify, formulate, and solve engineering and real-world problems effectively. PEO 3 Professional Communication and Interpersonal Skills: Demonstrate proficiency in oral, written, and technical communication, along with teamwork, leadership, and interpersonal skills. PEO 4 Ethical, Social, and Environmental Responsibility: Exhibit ethical behavior, professional integrity, and social responsibility while understanding environmental sustainability and human values. PEO 5 Innovation, Creativity, and Technological Adaptability: Engage in creative thinking and innovative problem-solving through hands-on exposure to modern tools such as Python, Arduino, Laser Cutting, and 3D Printing. PEO 6 Holistic Development and Lifelong Learning: Develop confidence, discipline, critical thinking, and a mindset for continuous improvement.
Program Outcomes (POs)
PO 1 Engineering Knowledge: Apply the knowledge of Mathematics, Science, Engineering fundamentals, and an engineering specialization to solve complex engineering problems. PO 2 Problem Analysis: Identify, formulate, review research literature, and analyze complex engineering problems using principles of mathematics and natural sciences. PO 3 Design/Development of Solutions: Design solutions for complex engineering problems with appropriate consideration for public health, safety, and environmental factors. PO 4 Conduct Investigations: Use research-based knowledge and methods including experiment design, data analysis, and synthesis of information. PO 5 Modern Tool Usage: Create, select, and apply appropriate techniques and modern engineering tools to complex engineering activities. PO 6 The Engineer and Society: Apply reasoning to assess societal, health, safety, legal, and cultural issues relevant to engineering practice. PO 7 Environment and Sustainability: Understand the impact of engineering solutions and demonstrate knowledge of sustainable development. PO 8 Ethics: Apply ethical principles and commit to professional ethics, responsibilities, and norms of engineering practice. PO 9 Individual and Teamwork: Function effectively as an individual and as a member or leader in diverse teams and multidisciplinary settings. PO 10 Communication: Communicate effectively on complex engineering activities, including writing effective reports, design documentation, and presentations. PO 11 Project Management and Finance: Demonstrate knowledge of engineering and management principles and apply them to manage projects. PO 12 Lifelong Learning: Recognize the need for independent and lifelong learning in the broadest context of technological change.
Program Specific Outcomes (PSOs)
PSO 1 Strong Scientific and Mathematical Foundation: Develop a deep understanding of the fundamental principles of Mathematics, Physics, and Chemistry for all engineering disciplines. PSO 2 Ability to Apply Basic Science to Engineering Problems: Apply mathematical formulations, scientific reasoning, and laboratory skills to model, analyze, and solve engineering-related problems. PSO 3 Effective Communication and Professional Skills: Demonstrate strong communication skills, teamwork, ethical behavior, and professional values. PSO 4 Experimental and Research Aptitude: Perform scientific experiments, analyze data accurately, and interpret results effectively, fostering research potential. PSO 5 Modern Tool Usage and Innovation Competence: Use modern tools and prototyping technologies — Python, Arduino, 3D Printing, Laser Cutting, simulation software — to create models and solve real-world engineering problems. PSO 6 Holistic Development with Ethical and Environmental Awareness: Exhibit ethical values, social responsibility, and environmental consciousness.
1. Engineering Physics Laboratory Equipment: Laser diffraction and interference kits, Optical benches, Newton's Rings apparatus, Spectrometers, Ultrasonic interferometer, Hall Effect setup, CROs, Semiconductor diode and transistor kits, Electronic timers, Magnetic field measurement devices.
2. Engineering Chemistry Laboratory Equipment: Digital pH meters, Conductivity meters, UV-visible spectrophotometer, Electrode potential setup, Colorimeters, Distillation and deionization units, Water analysis kits, Polymer and viscosity study apparatus, Corrosion study setups.
3. Mathematics and Computational Facility Software: Python for scientific computing, MATLAB/Octave, MS Excel, Desmos, GeoGebra, and online simulation tools.
4. Communication Skills Laboratory Facilities: Audio-visual systems, computers with language learning software, interview and group discussion simulation tools, microphones, headsets, projectors, and interactive screens.
5. Innovation Lab and Makerspace a) Arduino and IoT Kits: Arduino Uno/Mega boards, sensors (temperature, humidity, ultrasonic, gas, IR, LDR), actuators, servo/stepper motors, Wi-Fi modules. b) Python Programming Setup: Systems with Python 3.x, VS Code, PyCharm Community, numerical computation libraries. c) 3D Printing Facility: FDM 3D Printers (PLA/ABS compatible), Cura slicing software, model finishing tools. d) Laser Cutting and Engraving Machine: CO2 laser cutter compatible with acrylic, wood, MDF, cardboard, and light plastics.
6. Classrooms and ICT Facilities Projectors, smart boards, high-speed internet, audio systems, digital content delivery tools, and online learning platforms.

text:
Electrical & Electronics Engineering
Powering Progress Through Engineering
Est. Year
1980
Faculty
6
Students
35
About This Department
About Us
Electrical and Electronics Engineering (EEE) is a broad and dynamic branch of engineering that deals with the study, design, and application of electrical systems, electronic devices, and modern technological solutions. It covers two major areas: electrical engineering, which focuses on the generation, transmission, distribution, and utilization of electrical power; and electronics engineering, which involves the design and development of electronic circuits, semiconductor devices, communication systems, and embedded technologies. In this branch, students learn core subjects such as circuit theory, electrical machines, power systems, control systems, digital electronics, analog electronics, microprocessors, microcontrollers, signal processing, and electromagnetic fields.
EEE also extends into advanced fields like renewable energy systems, electric vehicles, automation, robotics, Internet of Things (IoT), power electronics, and smart grid technology. Electrical and Electronics engineers play an important role in modern society. They contribute to building and maintaining power plants, designing home appliances, developing communication networks, creating industrial automation systems, and supporting technological innovations in various sectors.
They work in industries such as power generation and distribution companies, manufacturing industries, electronics and semiconductor companies, IT and software firms, railways, aviation, telecommunications, research institutions, and government organizations. Because of its wide scope, EEE offers strong career opportunities in both core engineering fields and emerging technologies. It is a branch that combines theoretical knowledge with practical skills, enabling engineers to design efficient electrical systems and develop intelligent electronic solutions.
Overall, Electrical and Electronics Engineering is a versatile and future-oriented field that forms the backbone of modern infrastructure and technological advancement.
Department Information
Vision
To be a competent center of excellence in Electrical and Electronics Engineering, fostering education as per the need of technological advancements that contribute to sustainable development and improve the quality of life for society.
Mission
i) To cater fundamental knowledge in Electrical and Electronics Engineering. ii) To provide additional knowledge as per the changing technological requirement. iii) To prepare professionals with good morals and ethical values. iv) To collaborate with industry and research centres to enhance the technological skills of faculty and students. v) To encourage students to apply their skills to produce products useful for the society [SEED program].

title: Civil Engineering | AITM Bhatkal
text:
The Civil Engineering Department of AITM Bhatkal was established in 1980 and has played a key role in transforming the vision of the institute into reality.
The department offers a four-year full-time Bachelor of Engineering course in Civil Engineering with an intake of 30, affiliated with Visvesvaraya Technological University (VTU), Belagavi.
The department has qualified faculty, well-equipped laboratories, and very good computational facilities with application software like STAAD-Pro, ETABS, REVIT, and AutoCAD to cater to academic and research activities.
The department undertakes consultancy works in the areas of structural, geotechnical, and environmental engineering.
The department is recognized as a research center by VTU.
Since its establishment, the department has produced 13 university rank holders and four gold medalists.
Graduates are employed across India and abroad as Chief Engineers, Executive Engineers, Project Managers, and Assistant Engineers.
To become a centre of excellence in academics, research, and consultancy by imparting quality education and developing competent civil engineering professionals who will be sensitive, ethical, and dedicated to the development of society.
Mission
1. To deliver a quality engineering education through an innovative dynamic teaching-learning environment and impart professional experience.
2. To provide a platform for faculty and students for the application of innovative technical knowledge in their field of interest.
3. To develop professional skills in order to serve society by providing technical solutions to real-world problems.
Program Educational Objectives (PEOs)
PEO 1: To offer students a solid foundation in mathematical, scientific, and engineering basics that will allow them to address engineering problems as professionals. PEO 2: To provide solutions to a variety of civil engineering problems while taking into account new ideas, safety, cost effectiveness, and sustainability. PEO 3: To demonstrate leadership skills, engage in lifelong learning programs, and work collaboratively with diverse teams to meet social and ethical constraints. PEO 4: To inspire students to become successful entrepreneurs with ethical and societal responsibilities.
Program Outcomes (POs)
PO 1 Engineering Knowledge: Apply the knowledge of mathematics, science, engineering fundamentals, and an engineering specialization to the solution of complex engineering problems. PO 2 Problem Analysis: Identify, formulate, research literature, and analyse complex engineering problems using first principles. PO 3 Design/Development of Solutions: Design solutions for complex engineering problems with appropriate consideration for public health, safety, and environmental factors. PO 4 Conduct Investigations: Use research-based knowledge including design of experiments, analysis and interpretation of data. PO 5 Modern Tool Usage: Create, select, and apply appropriate techniques and modern engineering tools to complex engineering activities. PO 6 The Engineer and Society: Apply reasoning to assess societal, health, safety, legal, and cultural issues relevant to engineering practice. PO 7 Environment and Sustainability: Understand the impact of engineering solutions and the need for sustainable development. PO 8 Ethics: Apply ethical principles and commit to professional ethics and norms. PO 9 Individual and Team Work: Function effectively as an individual and as a member or leader in diverse teams and multidisciplinary settings. PO 10 Communication: Communicate effectively on complex engineering activities with the engineering community and society at large. PO 11 Project Management and Finance: Demonstrate knowledge of engineering and management principles and apply them to manage projects. PO 12 Life-long Learning: Recognise the need for independent and life-long learning in the broadest context of technological change.
Program Specific Outcomes (PSOs)
PSO 1: Graduates will have the ability to plan, analyse, design, execute and maintain cost-effective civil engineering structures without overexploitation of natural resources. PSO 2: Graduates will have the ability to take up employment, entrepreneurship, research and development for sustainable civil society. PSO 3: Graduates will be able to pursue opportunities for personal and professional growth, higher studies, demonstrate leadership skills and engage in lifelong learning by active participation in the civil engineering profession. PSO 4: Graduates will be able to demonstrate professional integrity and an appreciation of ethical, environmental, regulatory and issues related to civil engineering projects.
Laboratories: i) Concrete and Highway Laboratory ii) Geotechnical Engineering Laboratory iii) Environmental Engineering Laboratory iv) Building Material Testing Laboratory v) Surveying Laboratory vi) CAD Laboratory vii) Software Application Laboratory viii) BIM and CAD Laboratory ix) Fluid Mechanics and Irrigation Engineering Laboratory
The laboratories are equipped with modern digital instruments like Total Station, Ultrasonic Pulse Velocity Device, Rebound Hammer, and Digital Moisture Probe. Software: STAAD-Pro, ETABS, REVIT, AutoCAD.
Research Areas
Geotechnical Engineering, Structural Engineering.

title: Participation in Todays Human Chain Program | AITM
text:
Human Chain Program: A Symbol of Unity and Democracy
In a powerful display of unity and commitment to democratic values, students and faculty members from all institutions participated in today’s Human Chain Program. The event aimed to symbolize the strength of togetherness and the importance of standing for collective causes.
This initiative reflects our dedication to fostering a sense of civic responsibility and cooperation among the younger generation. By joining hands, participants demonstrated their solidarity and belief in the principles of democracy, equality, and communal harmony.
The event was a resounding success, with hundreds of students and faculty members actively participating, showcasing their enthusiasm and dedication. This human chain is not just a physical connection, but a reminder of how we are all bound by shared responsibilities and common goals.
Transport arrangements were made for female students, ensuring smooth participation for everyone involved. We are grateful to the authorities and the institutions for their support in making this event a meaningful and impactful one.
Together, we move forward, united in purpose and driven by the ideals of democracy and unity.
